learning_outcomes.text: Introduce non-specialist students to the fundamental electric circuit theory and its core applications.

Acquire basic knowledge and skills necessary for the analysis of electrical circuits in steady state and sinusoidal steady state, single phase and three phase, and static and rotating electrical machines.

syllabus_topics: Equivalences: Delta to Wye and Wye to Delta Conversion
Network Analysis: Nodal analysis and Mesh analysis
Representations of sinusoidal signals as a function of time, complex and phasor representation
Network components and their constitutive equations: Resistor, Capacitor, Inductor, Operational amplifier, Sources
Instantaneous Average and Reactive power, Complex power, Apparent power
Steady state network analysis: Nodal analysis and Mesh analysis
Magnetic fields in vacuum: Biot–Savart law, Ampère's law, Magnetic flux, self-inductance and mutual inductance
Electromagnetic induction: Lenz’s Law, Induced electromotive force (emf) and Magnetic forces on moving charges
Magnetic fields in materials: magnetic properties of materials (Diamagnetism, Paramagnetism, Ferromagnetism)
Transformer Ideal coupling and ideal transformer
assessment_rules: The assessment of learning outcomes attainment is performed through a written test and an oral interview. The written test involves solving one or more problems. The oral examination is only for students who achieved a score greater than 17/30 in the written test. The final score is an average of the results obtained in the written and oral tests.
bibliography: Fundamentals of Electric Circuits By Charles Alexander and Matthew Sadiku, McGraw Hill
degree: Laurea in Ingegneria Meccanica E Gestionale (First Level Degree In Mechanical And Management Engineering), classe L-9 Classe delle lauree in Ingegneria industriale
